text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, four activities that previously ran in every trace run in only about half of them: A22 in about 54 in 100 traces, and A31, A32 and A37 in about 47 in 100 each (all were 200 of 200 before). None of them repeats within a trace in either window, while A20, A21, A23 and A26 still appear in every trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, POS001, POS002, POS004, POS005]
- The later window shows two nearly mutually exclusive variants: A22 and the A31/A32/A37 group co-occur in only about 1 in 200 traces, and the three group members appear together in exactly the roughly 47 in 100 traces where any of them appears (in about 53 in 100 traces none of them is present). [REL011, REL012, REL013, REL020, REL021, REL022]
- Routing changed at two points: A20's outgoing transitions went from an roughly even split to A31, A32 and A37 (about 35, 34 and 31 in 100) to almost always A23 (about 995 in 1000); A21, previously always followed by A22, now leads to A22 in about 54 in 100 transitions and to A31, A32 or A37 in the rest (about 14–17 in 100 each). [DIR001, DIR002]
- The A31/A32/A37 group changed its successors: before, each sent roughly a third of its transitions to A23; in the later window they lead to each other and to A26, and transitions to A23 have nearly disappeared (about 1 in 100 from A32). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Order relations flipped: A31, A32 and A37 previously preceded A21, A23 and A22 in every trace; in the later window they follow A21 and A23, while A22 still precedes A26 and the group still precedes A26 when present. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL009, REL010, REL017, REL018, REL019]
- Event positions shifted: A31, A32 and A37 now occur later in the trace (mean relative position from about 0.40 to about 0.58), A23 earlier (about 0.45 to 0.39), A21 and A22 somewhat earlier, A20 slightly later. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]
- Step distances changed accordingly: A20 to A23 collapsed from 4 steps apart to 1 step in nearly all traces, and A21 to A26 is 2 steps in about 54 in 100 traces versus 4 steps in about 47 in 100; a few of the group's new distance comparisons rest on a single observed trace. [LAG001, LAG005, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process was restructured around a branch after A21: in the later window, about 47 in 100 traces run the A31/A32/A37 group (in varying internal order) between A21 and A26 and skip A22, while about 54 in 100 run A22 between A21 and A26 and skip the group; A20 now leads almost directly to A23, which sits earlier, instead of into the group. The 47 flagged items far exceed the roughly 0.5 expected by chance alone, and the placement aspect is shown directly — the group's order relations with A21 and A23 flip from "before" to "after", A20's successor changes, and the A20→A23 distance shrinks from 4 steps to 1 — rather than being inferred from participation counts alone. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL006, REL014, REL017, LAG001, LAG005]

Limitations: the branch shares are estimates from 200 traces per window, and a few traces deviate from the clean two-branch picture (one trace contains both A22 and the group, and one has A20 directly followed by A31). A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully rule out is that this branching behaviour existed before as a rare variant that the earlier 200-trace sample did not surface, since the before window shows the old pattern in all 200 traces; also, the occurrence, relation and position items partly reflect the same trace-level change, so their agreement is not independent confirmation. [REL011, REL012, REL013, DIR001, LAG002, LAG006]
